main_text.p: abolitas esse Leuiticas oblationes, qua nequaquam merebantur remissionem peccatorum, Hebræor. 10. 18. non negat vllam in veteri Testamento peccatorum remissionem fuisse, sed ostendit hanc, non typicis victimis, sed Agno Dei, qui tollit peccatu mundi, ex asse acceptam ferendam, esse: neciam oblationibus Leuiticis iam vllum esse locum posteaquam semel τὸ Λύτρον persoluit Christus.

Postremò, quando idem Gentium doctor ostendit, vetus Testamentu à nouo antiquatum & abolitum esse, Ceremonias, Sacramenta & Leuiticam liturgiam respicit: non autem communem vtriq; fœderi substantiam: ac, vt minore, quod dici solet: pomœrio circumscriba omnia, Legis pædagogia sublata, Euangelij libertatem & ministerium succesisse innuit.

Etsi autem, vt iam dicedi finem faciam, summa rerum maximarum fastigia mihi, in tanta temporis angustia vix licuit sectari: Spero tamen vobis viris sapientissimis et optimis etiā illud persuasum esse, quod alicubi præclarè dixit Bernardus: Nihil ita absq; labore manifestam facit veritatem, sicut breuis & pura narratio.

page.notes: Line-final "Oro" is set right-aligned at the foot as a catchword-like closing word; it is kept as a paragraph. Greek "τὸ Λύτρον" transcribed from the scan as printed; the Greek word is doubtful ("λύτρον" likely) and should be checked. The word "Hebræor." appears as printed. Possible printing error: "Testamentu à nouo" with "à" as printed. The word "vetus" and the form "Gentium" are as printed.
